# GitHub Copilot Instructions for Chat.LocalLLM

**Purpose:** Short, actionable guidance so an AI coding agent is immediately productive in this repository.

## Quick summary ✅
- Small Express-based TypeScript service exposing TSOA controllers (routes generated under `build/`).
- Dependency injection via `tsyringe` (IOC adapter in `src/lib/tsyringeTsoaIocContainer.ts`).
- Core business logic in `src/services/generator.service.ts` which uses `@huggingface/transformers` pipeline('text-generation', MODEL_ID).

## Quick start / common commands 🔧
- Install: npm install
- Build (generate TSOA types + compile): npm run build
  - This runs `tsoa routes && tsoa spec` then `tsc`.
- Dev (watch source → rebuild → restart): npm run dev
  - Uses `chokidar` and `nodemon`; watch rebuilds on `src` changes and restarts `dist/server.js`.
- Run produced build: npm run start (reads `local-node.env` via `--env-file`)
- Regenerate TSOA artifacts: npm run tsoa:gen

## Key files & what they show 📁
- `src/server.ts` — bootstraps Express, mounts TSOA-generated routes, serves Swagger UI in development.
- `src/controllers/*.ts` — TSOA controllers and route annotations (use these as source of truth for API surface).
- `src/services/generator.service.ts` — Hugging Face pipeline usage and where model calls happen.
- `src/models/generation.model.ts` — Types for Chat/Message/TextGenerationOutput used by API surface.
- `src/lib/tsyringeTsoaIocContainer.ts` — glues `tsyringe` DI to `tsoa`.
- `build/` — auto-generated by TSOA (`routes.ts`, `swagger.json`). Do not edit manually.
- `TODO.md` — repository-specific caveats (e.g., esbuild problems & model compatibility notes).

## Environment & secrets ⚠️
- Recognized env vars: `HF_TOKEN`, `HF_HOME`, `MODEL_ID`, `ENABLE_GPU`, `PORT`, `NODE_ENV`.
- Local env file: `local-node.env` is used for local runs (example exists in repo). **Do not commit secrets**; replace any tokens and rotate if present.
- Note: `GeneratorService` sets `env.cacheDir = HF_HOME` and will configure webgpu when `ENABLE_GPU=true`.

## API examples (use these exact endpoints) 💡
- GET default generation:
  - GET http://localhost:${PORT || 3000}/generator
- POST generate text (JSON body) — required shape: `{ "text": "Your prompt" }`
  - curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"text":"Hello"}' http://localhost:5560/generator
- Responses follow `TextGenerationOutput` (an array of `{ generated_text: string | Chat }`). See `src/models/generation.model.ts` for exact types.

## Project-specific patterns & constraints 🧭
- Controllers use TSOA decorators (`@Route`, `@Get`, `@Post`) and rely on TSOA-generated validators; **edit controllers, then re-run `npm run build`** to update `build/` artifacts.
- DI: controllers are registered/resolved via `tsyringe`. Use `@injectable()` and constructor injection when adding services.
- Do NOT edit files in `build/`; they are generated and will be overwritten.
- Build uses `tsc` because TypeScript configuration enables `emitDecoratorMetadata` and `experimentalDecorators` (see `tsconfig.json`). Note: esbuild was attempted but flagged in `TODO.md` as not suitable for decorator metadata.

## Known issues / TODOs (from `TODO.md`) ⚠️
- Some Hugging Face models may not be compatible with local transformers runtime; check `TODO.md` before swapping `MODEL_ID`.
- There is a note that esbuild does not emit decorator metadata; use `tsc` to avoid runtime-decorator issues.

## Guidance for AI agents (how to safely change code) 🤖
- If you modify controller signatures or models, ensure you re-run `npm run build` to regenerate routes and spec.
- Avoid touching `build/` files directly; update sources and re-generate.
- Flag any discovered secrets (like HF tokens) and request remediation rather than auto-committing them.
- When optimizing `GeneratorService`, respect that pipeline init returns a Promise and is cached on the service instance.
